outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the freeness part has acquired a withdrawn 2024 claimed proof (Chan) and a September 2026 manuscript released in OpenAI's openai/math repository that claims a full proof in every dimension, with no Lean link and no expert check found; partial results (Han 2026 linear bound, Siu's 2026 very-ampleness article with a weaker bound, text unreadable to me) and the 2014–2020 dimension-5 results sit alongside.
problem_asks: Frozen statement: for a positive holomorphic line bundle L on a compact complex manifold M, with canonical bundle K_M, the bundle K_M tensor L^m, and its behaviour as m grows. Unpacked: (a) global generation (freeness) of K_M tensor L^m for every m at or above a threshold; (b) very ampleness of K_M tensor L^m for every m at or above a threshold. Quantifiers: every compact complex manifold M of every dimension n, and every positive L. Note: the frozen statement text does not give the thresholds. I took the standard thresholds m >= n+1 for (a) and m >= n+2 for (b) from the current Wikipedia article (fetched) because the bullet names the conjecture. Also: a positive holomorphic L on a compact complex manifold makes M projective (Kodaira embedding); literature works with smooth projective varieties. That reduction is mine, not a source's.

events.what_happened: Reider's theorem (Annals of Mathematics 127 (1988) 309-316): for a nef divisor D on a smooth projective surface, a criterion for |K+D| to be base-point free (D^2 > 4) and very ample (D^2 > 8). Applied to D = mL it gives the surface case: K+3L globally generated and K+4L very ample. Surfaces only.
events.delivers: Both parts of the conjecture for surfaces (n = 2): global generation for m >= 3 and very ampleness for m >= 4 for ample L.
events.remains: Every dimension n >= 3.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in dimension 2.

events.what_happened: Ein and Lazarsfeld, Global generation of pluricanonical and adjoint linear series on smooth projective threefolds, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 6(4) (1993) 875-903. Proves global generation of K+4L on smooth projective threefolds (freeness part, n = 3).
events.delivers: Global generation part for n = 3 (m >= 4). Per Wikipedia and the Han and OpenAI texts.
events.remains: Very ampleness for n = 3; all n other than 3 from this result.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society

events.time_since_posted: 33 years (journal year; preprint date not found)
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in dimension 3 (freeness part).

events.what_happened: Angehrn and Siu, Effective freeness and point separation for adjoint bundles, preprint December 1994, Invent. Math. 122 (1995) 291-308. Analytic method giving effective global generation of K+mL for all m at or above a quadratic threshold, plus point separation.
events.revisions: Preprint December 1994 (per reference lists); journal Invent. Math. 1995.
events.delivers: Effective global generation for m >= (n^2+n+2)/2 (threshold as quoted by Han 2026 and Ghidelli-Lacini). Takayama (1997, via a search summary) quotes m > n(n+1)/2 for the same result; I could not reconcile the two.
events.remains: The sharp threshold m >= n+1 in every dimension n >= 4 from this result; very ampleness.

checked_by.where: Reference details from search results (not opened)

events.doubts: Threshold discrepancy: (n^2+n+2)/2 in Han 2026 and Ghidelli-Lacini versus n(n+1)/2 in Takayama's 1997 note as reported in a search summary. Unresolved; original not opened.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in a weaker, quadratic form.

events.what_happened: Helmke, On Fujita's conjecture, Duke Math. J. 88(2) (1997) 201-216. Induction method giving a quadratic effective bound for global generation of adjoint bundles (as described by Han 2026, which cites it).
events.delivers: Effective global generation with a quadratic threshold in n (secondary description). Not the conjecture's linear threshold.
events.remains: The sharp n+1 threshold and very ampleness.

Hypotheses on the abstract page: L^5 > 7^5 and L^d . Z >= 7^d for subvarieties Z of dimension 1 <= d <= 4. Conclusion: O_X(K_X+L) is globally generated.

events.what_happened: Ye and Zhu, On Fujita's freeness conjecture in dimension 5, arXiv 1511.09154 (30 Nov 2015, single version); published Advances in Mathematics 371 (2020) 107210 (DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2020.107210). The arXiv abstract page states: 'Let X be a smooth projective variety of dimension 5 and L be an ample line bundle on X. We show that |K_X+6L| is base-point free.' Secondary summaries of the published main theorem give a different form (|K_X+L| under L^d . Z >= 6^d) and an appendix by Jun Lu.
events.revisions: Single version on arXiv; published 2020 in Adv. Math.
events.delivers: Per the arXiv abstract as fetched: freeness part for n = 5 (m = 6) for any ample L on smooth projective 5-folds, no volume hypothesis. Per a search summary of the 2020 published main theorem: a volume-hypothesis version concluding |K_X+L| base-point free. The two statements do not obviously agree; see doubts.
events.remains: n >= 6, and for the published version possibly the unhypothesised case, depending on which form is correct.
events.doubts: The arXiv abstract's |K_X+6L| for any ample L and the published main theorem as reported in a search summary (|K_X+L| under L^d . Z >= 6^d) differ. ScienceDirect (publisher page) returned 403, so I could not settle which the published version states. Han 2026 and OpenAI 2026 both treat dimension 5 as known. Han's bibliography cites this result as 'Ye-Zhang 2017, 2020', which appears to be a citation-key error.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in dimension 5 (freeness part, m = n+1 = 6), per the arXiv abstract.

events.what_happened: Jingjun Han, A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture, arXiv 2609.01574 (v1 1 Sep 2026; v2 11 Sep 2026). Proves K_X + mL globally generated for every m >= ceil(C_0 n), C_0 = 1.77629988..., for smooth complex projective X of dimension n with ample L; corollary K_X + 2nL globally generated. Introduction treats the conjecture as open ('the conjectural bound' n+1). Acknowledgements: 'The author thanks ChatGPT 5.6 Pro for suggesting the examples in Appendix A' (v2; v1 has 'Remark A.3') and 'for assistance with English editing'.

For every n >= 2 this threshold is larger than n+1 (n=2: 4 against 3; n=3: 6 against 4), so it reaches the sharp statement in no dimension n >= 2; for n = 1 it coincides with n+1.
events.remains: The sharp m >= n+1 threshold for every n >= 2; very ampleness.
events.direction: Partial; supports the conjecture with a weaker, linear bound.

events.what_happened: Antonio Laface, Fujita freeness for projectivized toric vector bundles, arXiv 2608.28438 (28 Aug 2026, single version). For a smooth projective toric variety X of dimension n and a toric vector bundle E of rank r, the projective bundle Y = P(E) with ample A: K_Y + mA globally generated under ma >= r and m delta(A) > n (delta a positive integer from degrees on invariant curves). Claims every projectivized toric vector bundle satisfies Fujita's freeness conjecture.
events.revisions: Single version.
events.delivers: Freeness part for one class: projectivizations of toric vector bundles over smooth projective toric varieties, under the numerical conditions above.
events.remains: Y of other types. Note: dim Y = n+r-1, and the conjecture for Y asks m >= n+r. The fetched summary gives the Fujita-type choice as m >= n+1 with n = dim X; I could not reconcile this with dim Y, and did not read the main theorem.
events.doubts: Threshold apparently taken with n = dim X rather than dim Y; unresolved from the summary.
events.direction: Toward the conjecture, on a restricted class of toric projective bundles.

events.what_happened: OpenAI, 'Fujita's freeness conjecture', manuscript preprints/Fujitas-freeness-conjecture-September-23-2026 in the openai/math repository, dated 23 Sep 2026, author line 'OpenAI'. Abstract: 'We prove Fujita's freeness conjecture. If X is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n and L is an ample line bundle, then K_X+mL is globally generated for every integer m >= n+1.' Main theorem: for smooth connected projective X over C of dimension n >= 1 and ample L, K_X+(n+1)L is generated by global sections; corollary for all m >= n+1. The repository catalogue lists family 038 'Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension', with one manuscript and no Lean link. The repository was published on GitHub around 6-7 Oct 2026 (press reports disagree).
events.revisions: Manuscript self-dated 23 Sep 2026; public release on GitHub reported 6-7 Oct 2026; repository history (7 Oct) records three withdrawn manuscripts on Hodge conjecture topics and no Fujita entry.
events.delivers: As stated: global generation of K_X+mL for all m >= n+1, all n >= 1, smooth connected complex projective X and ample L. This is the freeness part only; the abstract and main theorem do not claim very ampleness. The reduction from the frozen statement (compact complex manifolds with positive L) to smooth projective varieties with ample L follows from Kodaira's embedding theorem; that step is mine, not the manuscript's.
events.remains: Very ampleness (m >= n+2) is not claimed in the abstract or main theorem.
events.doubts: No expert engagement with this entry found in my searches; press coverage of the release is critical of verification and attribution in general (including comments attributed to Terence Tao), but none names this entry. The repository says that unformalized results 'could have issues' and that 'Not all have accompanying Lean formalizations'. The entry has no Lean link; lean/formalization.yaml contains no Fujita entry (read via a summarising fetch). I read the LaTeX section outlines (preliminaries, minimization, centers, isolation) through a summarising fetch; the mathematics was not checked. The outlines describe: minimizers of monomial test pairs with attainment and discrepancy bounds; a contradiction on centres using a discrete Brunn-Minkowski count; and an isolation argument at a closed point; cited inputs include Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing, Wlodarczyk resolution, Demailly-Kollar, Lazarsfeld-Mustata, Kaveh-Khovanskii, Howald, Gardner, Fujino and Fujita 1993. No specific error identified.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: claims the freeness part in every dimension, at the sharp bound.

events.what_happened: The family has one manuscript, 'Fujita's freeness conjecture' (OpenAI, dated September 23, 2026). Its main theorem: for X a smooth connected projective variety over ℂ of dimension n ≥ 1 and L an ample line bundle on X, Kₓ + (n+1)L is generated by its global sections. A corollary (cor:all-powers) deduces that Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every integer m ≥ n+1, by applying the main theorem to X × ℙʳ with r = m−n−1 and the ample bundle L ⊠ O(1); the adjoint bundle there is (Kₓ + mL) ⊠ O(n), and its restriction to X × {z} is Kₓ + mL. The text gives ℙⁿ with L = O(1) as the sharpness example: Kₓ + (n+1)L is trivial while Kₓ + nL has no nonzero sections. The proof is by contradiction at a point x. (i) An 'ordinary-order alternative' shows that failure of generation at x forces a strict asymptotic inequality for the mean ordinary order of bases of H⁰(X, mL). (ii) The proof minimizes an exponential functional over bases of H⁰(X, mL) and weighted monomial valuations whose centers contain x, for a fixed t < n+1. It shows the minimum is attained and has bounded discrepancy. (iii) A tangential variation of a minimizer, a uniform lower estimate on restriction spaces, and a discrete Brunn–Minkowski inequality show that minimizers have center exactly {x} in arbitrarily large degrees. (iv) A rational supporting profile is used to build an effective SNC boundary and a reduced divisor S over x on which the boundary coefficient equals the log discrepancy and is strictly smaller on neighbouring components. (v) Kawamata–Viehweg vanishing, in Fujino's logarithmic form, lifts a nonzero value from S, and descent gives a section of Kₓ + (n+1)L that is nonzero at x. This contradicts the assumed failure.
events.delivers: For the freeness (global generation) part of the list's problem: for every smooth complex projective variety X of dimension n and every ample L on X, Kₓ + mL is globally generated for every m ≥ n+1. The threshold n+1 is the sharp one, per the sharpness example. Restrictions: the setting is smooth projective varieties over ℂ, not compact complex manifolds with a positive holomorphic bundle; L must be ample; the theorem assumes connectedness, which the text says only fixes notation (applies componentwise). The manuscript states its result as a proof of Fujita's freeness conjecture. Its freeness statement matches part (a) of the list's problem, at threshold m ≥ n+1. The manuscript does not claim the whole problem as the list words it: the list's problem also covers very ampleness (part (b)), which the Introduction says is not asserted. The list's compact-complex-manifold formulation is not addressed in the manuscript. The research pass's reduction (a positive holomorphic bundle on a compact complex manifold makes it projective via Kodaira's embedding theorem, with L ample) would bring it into scope, but the manuscript does not state this reduction.
events.remains: Part (b) of the problem: very ampleness of Kₓ + mL for m ≥ n+2, using the research pass's threshold. The Introduction explicitly says the manuscript does not assert separation of points or tangent directions, or the very-ampleness part of Fujita's conjecture. The compact-complex-manifold formulation is not treated directly in the text. Nothing is claimed for m ≤ n, and the sharpness example shows that m = n cannot work in general.
events.doubts: (1) Several steps are given in condensed form. The constructibility half of the closed-threshold-locus lemma (lem:lct-family) is argued by saying it parallels the proof of Demailly–Kollár, with a stratification sketched in a few sentences. The multiplicity bound in lem:min-initials is justified in two sentences via a general curve. The claim that every fixed ball meets j⁻¹Hⱼ along the subsequence, which the ordinary-order alternative relies on, is argued in one paragraph without explicit constants. The compactness step in the existence of minimizers asserts that section orders are linear in the weights on the fixed model. (2) The final lift is described as following the discrepancy-and-vanishing strategy of Fujita 1993, §1(1.6), but the text writes out the lift itself and does not separately verify the adaptation. (3) The claim is much stronger than the bounds the Introduction itself cites. The sharpest general bounds it lists are of order n: Han, m ≥ ⌈C₀n⌉ with C₀ ≈ 1.776, and Ghidelli–Lacini, m ≥ n(log log n + 2.34) for n ≥ 2. The Introduction says the sharp bound is known for curves, for surfaces (Reider), and for dimensions three to five (Ein–Lazarsfeld, Kawamata, Ye–Zhu). The all-dimension claim is stated without hedging. (4) The Introduction records that a 2024 preprint by Chan, claiming a stronger intersection-number form, was withdrawn because a local extension argument did not guarantee the required vanishing order. The manuscript's final step is also a vanishing-based extension from a divisor over x. The text does not say explicitly how that failure is avoided beyond the isolation lemma. (5) The abstract does not state the connectedness hypothesis that the main theorem includes. The text says this only fixes notation, which I take at its word.
events.direction: proves the freeness conjecture (global generation) at the sharp threshold m ≥ n+1; the very-ampleness part is not addressed

disputes.summary: OpenAI's manuscript describes Chan's withdrawn preprint as announcing a proof of a 'stronger intersection-number formulation', whereas Chan's v1 abstract, as fetched, states the freeness statement m >= dim X + 1 directly. Which formulation Chan claimed is not settled by my reading.

summary: The freeness part has two claimed full proofs and one partial result since 2024. Chan's preprint (arXiv 2411.07129, 11 Nov 2024) claimed it for all dimensions; the author withdrew v2 on 24 Nov 2024 after Helmke pointed out, in the arXiv comment, that the construction of f^loc need not give a section of the required vanishing order. OpenAI's repository (openai/math, released around 6-7 Oct 2026) lists family 038 'Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension'; the manuscript (self-dated 23 Sep 2026, author 'OpenAI') states the claim for smooth complex projective varieties and all m >= n+1, with no Lean link and no public expert check that I could find. I confirmed the entry and its claim from CONTENTS.md, the repository README, and the manuscript's LaTeX main file and section list; I read the section outlines through a summarising fetch and did not verify the mathematics. Han (arXiv 2609.01574, 1 and 11 Sep 2026) proves m >= ceil(1.776 n) and treats the conjecture as open; the bound is above n+1 for every n >= 2, so it is partial. Siu's 2026 article in Acta Math. Sinica (online 15 May 2026) claims very ampleness with a weaker bound, dated to the journal write-up per the first-public-argument rule, but its text was unreadable to me. Dimensions up to five are classically covered for the freeness part (Reider 1988 for surfaces; Ein-Lazarsfeld 1993 for threefolds; Kawamata 1997 for fourfolds per secondary sources; Ye-Zhu for fivefolds). Close calls: whether the OpenAI entry counts as a resolution or an unchecked claim; the AI attribution, which for the OpenAI entry rests on the repository's 'vast majority' sentence rather than a per-manuscript statement; and whether Han's ChatGPT 5.6 Pro acknowledgement, which suggested sharpness examples in an appendix that Han says does not feed the main theorem, is load-bearing. Source discrepancies are recorded in the events: Ye-Zhu's 2015 abstract (|K_X+6L| for any ample L) against the 2020 published main theorem as reported in a search summary (|K_X+L| under a volume hypothesis); Angehrn-Siu's threshold (n^2+n+2)/2 against Takayama's n(n+1)/2; Ghidelli-Lacini's constant 2.34 against 3; and Han's citation key 'Ye-Zhang 2017, 2020' against a paper by Ye and Zhu. Quotes from PDFs and from the OpenAI LaTeX are as returned by the fetch tool and were not byte-checked, because scratch copies outside the project need approval.
competing_reading: Read the OpenAI family 038 manuscript as a complete proof of the freeness part in every dimension, as the repository catalogue states, and count the freeness part as settled by AI output, with the model attribution taken from the repository's statement that the results were produced by an internal OpenAI model. On this reading Chan's 2024 claim is a withdrawn precursor, Han's linear bound is partial, and the dimension-5 history is consistent. The opposite reading: a single unrefereed, unformalized, humanly unchecked claim whose AI attribution is collection-wide ('the vast majority') and not stated for this manuscript, so that nothing is settled as of 10 Oct 2026, and the Fujita entry should be counted as a claim rather than a resolution.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A qualified expert's public check of the 23 Sep 2026 manuscript, especially its minimization, centers and isolation sections, or a Lean proof of family 038 with a statement matching the freeness conjecture; (2) a per-manuscript provenance statement for family 038 from openai/math saying whether the model produced it and whether any human checked it; (3) the text of Siu's Acta Math. Sinica article, with its abstract and its m(n) bound, and whether it covers all n; (4) the published Advances in Mathematics 2020 main theorem of Ye-Zhu, to see whether it carries a volume hypothesis and concludes |K_X+L| or |K_X+6L|; (5) the exact statements of Angehrn-Siu's and Heier's theorems; (6) whether any of Han's appendix examples is used beyond Corollary A.2, and the exact wording of Han's acknowledgement in the arXiv source.

event.what_happened: Antonio Laface, Fujita freeness for projectivized toric vector bundles, arXiv 2608.28438 (28 Aug 2026, single version). For a smooth projective toric variety X of dimension n and a toric vector bundle E of rank r, the projective bundle Y = P(E) with ample A: K_Y + mA globally generated under ma >= r and m delta(A) > n (delta a positive integer from degrees on invariant curves). Claims every projectivized toric vector bundle satisfies Fujita's freeness conjecture.
event.delivers: Freeness part for one class: projectivizations of toric vector bundles over smooth projective toric varieties, under the numerical conditions above.
event.remains: Y of other types. Note: dim Y = n+r-1, and the conjecture for Y asks m >= n+r. The fetched summary gives the Fujita-type choice as m >= n+1 with n = dim X; I could not reconcile this with dim Y, and did not read the main theorem.
event.doubts: Threshold apparently taken with n = dim X rather than dim Y; unresolved from the summary.
event.direction: Toward the conjecture, on a restricted class of toric projective bundles.

judgement.why: The statement names the Fujita conjecture, which has two parts (freeness at m >= n+1, very ampleness at m >= n+2), so a proof of freeness alone is a case (F3), not whole; the OpenAI manuscript explicitly disclaims very ampleness. openai-2026 and openai-math-038 are the same manuscript recorded twice and get identical answers. It is unreviewed and doubtful but not not_credible: there is no identified error, and three to eight days of silence is too short to count as missing uptake. Its AI role is generated: the repository says the manuscripts were produced by an internal model, and the author line is just 'OpenAI'. The basis is a collection-level 'vast majority' sentence, though. Han's ChatGPT acknowledgement covers sharpness examples for an appendix corollary that the main bound (Theorem 1.1) does not use, so the bound event is none. Chan is knocked_down by withdrawal. Siu 2026 is treated as a very-ampleness bound and counted digested because a journal of record published it. Conditional results (BBMT, Benammar) are none. Different-setting results (char p, 2K+mL, convex Fujita numbers, the K+aK+bL variant, singular T-varieties, the m=1 volume-hypothesis result) are variant. Dimension-specific proofs are case and sharp-threshold-in-n bounds are bound.
judgement.doubts: AI attribution for the OpenAI manuscript rests on a repository-wide 'vast majority' sentence, not a per-manuscript statement. Han's ai_role is a close call: ChatGPT suggested constructions that appear in the paper (assisted on a strict reading), but they support only a sharpness corollary, not the freeness bound that bears on this problem. Siu 2026's content is unread, so its scope as a bound is inferred from a talk abstract. The reduction from compact complex manifolds with positive L to projective varieties via Kodaira is the researcher's, though it is standard.
